title: "SVM: Classical and Quantum Kernel Classifiers"
description: "A three-part series: from the SVM margin to a side-by-side comparison of classical and quantum kernels."
toc: false
---

This SVM series builds from first principles to a head-to-head comparison of classical and quantum kernel classifiers.
Each notebook follows the same pattern: mathematics first, then code.

::: {.lesson-grid}
::: {.lesson-card}
### [1. Support Vector Machines](1.0-svm.ipynb)

Derive the maximum-margin hyperplane, read the primal and dual forms of the SVM, and control the soft-margin trade-off with $C$.

**Prerequisites:** vectors, inner products, and basic Python.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [2. Kernels in Support Vector Machines](2.0-kernel.ipynb)

Understand feature maps, the kernel trick, and the kernel SVM decision function through polynomial and RBF examples.

**Prerequisites:** [1. Support Vector Machines](1.0-svm.ipynb).
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [3. SVM: Classical and Quantum Kernel Classifiers](3.0-classical-vs-quantum.ipynb)

Compare a classical RBF kernel and a quantum feature-map kernel side by side on the same dataset using the same support-vector learning rule.

**Prerequisites:** [2. Kernels in SVMs](2.0-kernel.ipynb).
:::
:::
